notes:
Summary: Stalled → closed-lost.

Background:
- Vertical: industrial manufacturing — line-side visual QA, anomaly detection on camera feeds.
- Requirement: fully on-prem, physically air-gapped inference; no outbound telemetry or control-plane phone-home allowed; HSM-backed keying; long-term retention/erase controls.

Timeline & activities (shorthand):
- 2025-09-12: Intro call (Jordan) — initial fit, interest in reducing inference latency on camera clusters.
- 2025-10-03: Technical deep-dive w/ security (Fireflies ff_2025-10-03_choquant). Security defined air-gap as mandatory.
- 2025-11-18: Lab PoC started — local nodes deployed; inference latency within target; cost model reviewed.
- 2026-01-20: Security review escalated; procurement asked for appliance-only option; Redwood Private requires at least intermittent control-plane connectivity for updates/metrics.
- 2026-02-15: Customer notified selection of appliance vendor (HavenAI Appliances); procurement moved to capex. Final call (ff_2026-02-15_security_review).

Customer quotes (paraphrase):
- "We cannot have any external telemetry or phone-home for lifecycle management." — Head of Security.
- "If it's not appliance-based, it's a non-starter." — CIO.

Why we lost / blockers:
- Primary: strict air-gapped/on-prem appliance requirement — Redwood's Private offering still expects a management/control plane path; security team would not accept.
- Secondary: procurement policy shift to capex (one-time appliance buy) and vendor offered on-site HSM integration and maintenance.
- No strong internal champion after Head of Automation left in Dec '25.

Internal next steps / recommended follow-up:
- Mark closed-lost; capture specific technical gaps (ticket INF-4821 filed).
- Product: evaluate feasibility of an offline appliance SKU or fully offline lifecycle mode (engineering ask).
- AE: monitor for policy changes; target re-engagement window 6-9 months.

Attachments: pricing deck, security FAQ linked.

AE notes: SE Priya Singh heavily involved on PoC. Sales played standard plays; technical fit was good but deployment constraint (air-gap/appliance) was absolute.
